predecessors.name: Kingdom of the Franks
predecessors.text: the Frankish lands east of the Rhine: Saxony, Austrasia, Alamannia, Bavaria and the March of Carinthia, with Speyer, Worms and Mainz on the left bank (Treaty of Verdun, August 843)

successors.name: Kingdom of Germany
successors.text: East Francia under Conrad I, elected 10 November 911; Lotharingia broke away in November 911 (west-franks dossier)

rulers.name: Louis the Younger
rulers.title: king in Saxony, Franconia and Thuringia; also Bavaria from 879/880 (joint heir)

rulers.name: Charles the Fat
rulers.title: king in Alamannia from 876; sole king of East Francia from 882

ledger.x: 843: the Treaty of Verdun gives Louis the German the eastern Frankish lands.
844: Louis the German subjects the Obotrites.
869: Lothair II dies and his uncles quarrel over his realm.
870: Meerssen ends the contest for Lotharingia, 8 August.
870: Meerssen gives Louis the German the east of Lothair II's realm.
876: Charles the Bald invades East Francia after Louis the German's death (28 August).
876: 8 October, Louis the Younger beats the West Franks at Andernach.
880: Ribemont gives western Lotharingia to East Francia.
884: Svatopluk of Great Moravia swears fidelity to Charles the Fat.
888: the Transjurane magnates elect Rudolph I and Upper Burgundy leaves East Francia.
888: Rudolph I claims Lotharingia.
892, July: the oath of 884 is broken and Arnulf invades Moravia.
894: the fighting between Rudolph and Arnulf ends.
894: Arnulf takes Lombardy.
895: Bohemia leaves Great Moravia for Arnulf.
895, May: Arnulf cuts Lotharingia out of East Francia as a kingdom for his son Zwentibold.
895, May: Lotharingia becomes a sub-kingdom under the East Frankish crown.
896: Arnulf takes Rome and is crowned emperor.
896, from April: Arnulf's Italy slips away.

896, from April: the fighting for Italy ends in Berengar's and Lambert's favour after Formosus's death (4 April 896): 'For the rest of his life Arnulf exercised very little control in Italy' (no further campaign on the page).
900: the Hungarians occupy Pannonia.
900, 13 August: Zwentibold is overthrown and killed.
900: Lotharingia returns to Louis the Child on Zwentibold's death (13 August); in 903 he appointed Gebhard duke ('duke of the kingdom that many call Lothair's').
911: the dossier ends and with it the bridging end of the Obotrite tribute (844).
911: the dossier ends and with it the bridging end of Bohemia's vassalage (895).
911: the Carolingian line of East Francia ends and the kingdom passes to Conrad I.

wars.name: Louis the German's invasion of West Francia
wars.outcome: Louis invaded in 858 and issued a charter dated the first year of his reign in West Francia; the campaign failed through desertion and the loyalty of the Aquitanian bishops, and the brothers swore peace at Koblenz on 7 June 860.

wars.name: Contest for Lothair II's kingdom
wars.outcome: Treaty of Meerssen, 8 August 870: Louis the German takes the east of Lotharingia (Aachen, Metz, most of Frisia, most of Upper Burgundy); Charles the Bald the west and Lower Burgundy.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's invasion of East Francia
wars.outcome: Charles was beaten by Louis the Younger at Andernach on 8 October 876; no ground was kept.

wars.name: Louis the Younger's West Frankish succession bid and the Treaty of Ribemont
wars.outcome: Fourons (November 878), the invasion as far as Verdun (879) and Ribemont (February 880): East Francia keeps the whole of Lotharingia; the West Frankish border set then 'stayed largely the same until the Late Middle Ages'.

wars.name: Wilhelminer War
wars.outcome: A war in the March of Pannonia, 'ran from 882 to 884' (Charles the Fat page); the page gives no result and no border moved.

wars.name: Arnulf's war with Rudolph I of Upper Burgundy
wars.outcome: Rudolph claimed the whole of Lotharingia after his election in 888 and took much of modern Lorraine and Alsace; Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; hostilities 'seem to have continued…

wars.name: Arnulf's Moravian campaigns
wars.outcome: Arnulf failed to conquer Great Moravia in 892, 893 and 899; he gained part of its land around 893-894 (western Hungary, already inside the shape); in 899 'he used Magyar help to impose some control over Moravia'.

wars.name: Arnulf's Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: January 894 Bergamo, Milan and Pavia taken; October 1895 second campaign; Rome on 21 February 896 and imperial coronation on 22 February; a stroke and Lambert's and Berengar's counter-moves ended Arnulf's control in 896.

wars.name: Magyar invasions of East Francia
wars.outcome: Magyars ravaged Bavaria in 900 and Saxony twice in 906; in 907 they defeated the Bavarians at Pressburg (killing Margrave Luitpold) and in 910 beat Louis the Child's army at Augsburg.

certainty.note: The Verdun lines in the west are described by rivers and regions, not surveyed; the eastern marches (Carinthia, Pannonia, the Slav frontier on the Elbe) are soft throughout.

The frontier with West Francia is treaty-fixed from Meerssen (870, 'the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saone and Rhone', west-franks dossier) and Ribemont (880) and is the sharp exception; the Slav, Moravian, Bohemian and Magyar frontiers stay…
